text:
Pittsburgh has lost five straight, is 2-8-0 in its last ten and sits at 7-15-2, with a 4% chance at the playoffs by our numbers. Some of that is cruel. The Penguins have scored almost 11 fewer goals than their chances predict and sit nearly nine points below what their play deserved. But the slide is partly real: they got 47% of the expected goals in the losing streak, and Arturs Silovs has gone 0-5-0 at .845.

Everyone knows where this is going. The beat reporter Josh Yohe was quoted by Markerzone saying Erik Karlsson and Rickard Rakell are about to be traded, and Ottawa's GM was in the building. Ryan Wilson put it plainly on Bluesky: the Penguins are obviously selling. Sidney Crosby's future has its own headline cycle, and Evgeni Malkin has been out hurt.

What is left to watch is the next group. Connor Dewar, Blake Lizotte and Nick Robertson have quietly been the best line by goals (4-1), Samuel Girard and Kaedan Korczak the busiest pair, and Ben Kindel, the rookie, is part of what Dan Muse's staff is building toward. A team this far below its expected points will win more games than it has. The question is whether Crosby, Karlsson and Rakell are still here when it does.
headline: The Penguins are sellers now
